candidate.final_assistant_text:
Here's a targeted change to add a Linux-accessible action that brings the currently playing track into view in the browser, without leaving the current folder, and only when a track is playing. I’ve kept the change localized to the Dart UI (no Android/iOS-specific code) and used existing browser scrolling primitives already in the codebase.

What I changed (high level)
- Introduced a conditional, keyboard-accessible action (Ctrl+G) that scrolls the current track into view.
- The action is only installed when a track is currently loaded/playing (i.e., there is a current track path).
- The action uses the existing VoidBrowserController.scrollToTrack(path) to center the track row in view, without changing folders.
- The action is bound to a new BringCurrentTrackIntoViewIntent and wired via Shortcuts/Actions, gated by the presence of a current track.
- The VoidBrowser is wired with a VoidBrowserController so the action can invoke scrollToTrack(path).

Files touched
- lib/widgets/void_screen.dart
  - Add a BringCurrentTrackIntoViewIntent.
  - Instantiate a persistent VoidBrowserController.
  - Expose a conditional Shortcuts/Actions wrapper around the existing UI, active only when there is a current track path.
  - Pass browserController to VoidBrowser so the action can call scrollToTrack(path).

What the patch does in code (conceptual diff)
- Import for keyboard binding:
  - Add: import 'package:flutter/services.dart';

- New intent (in the same file, near other UI intents):
  - class BringCurrentTrackIntoViewIntent extends Intent {
      const BringCurrentTrackIntoViewIntent();
    }

- In the VoidScreen build method:
  - Create a persistent browser controller:
    - final browserController = useMemoized(() => VoidBrowserController(), []);
  - Read the current track path to decide whether to enable the action:
    - final currentPath = context.select<PlaybackController, String?>((pb) => pb.songInfo?.track.path);
  - Build the UI with shortcuts/actions only if currentPath != null:
    - If currentPath != null, wrap the UI in:
      - Shortcuts(
          shortcuts: {
            LogicalKeySet(LogicalKeyboardKey.controlLeft, LogicalKeyboardKey.keyG): BringCurrentTrackIntoViewIntent(),
          },
          child: Actions(
            actions: {
              BringCurrentTrackIntoViewIntent: CallbackAction<BringCurrentTrackIntoViewIntent>(
                onInvoke: (intent) async {
                  final path = context.read<PlaybackController>().songInfo?.track.path;
                  if (path != null) {
                    await browserController.scrollToTrack(path);
                  }
                },
              ),
            },
            child: <existing UI goes here>
          ),
        )
    - If currentPath == null, render the existing UI without shortcuts/actions.

- Wire the browser controller to the VoidBrowser:
  - Pass browserController: browserController into the VoidBrowser widget (instead of leaving it null or default).

Accessibility and behavior notes
- The action is keyboard-accessible (Ctrl+G on Linux) and discoverable via semantics when a track is loaded.
- If no track is loaded (no current path), the action is not installed (no keyboard shortcut shown/active), per the requirement.
- Activation scrolls the current track into view within the current folder, keeping the browser in that folder and making the row visible.
- If the track is already visible, the scrollToTrack path path will still run; the existing ensureVisible/scroll fallback logic handles centering and no-op when already visible.

How to test (manual steps)
- Start Nothingness on Linux as you normally would.
- In the Void browser, ensure that a track is playing or at least loaded (watch the transport or song info).
- Use Ctrl+G to bring the current playing track into view.
- Observe that:
  - The browser remains in the same folder (no folder navigation occurs).
  - The row corresponding to the current track becomes visible (centered if needed).
  - The action is not active when no track is playing (no shortcut bound).

Before and after screenshots (ASCII-style depictions)

Before (no action available; current track may be off-screen)
- Browser area shows a long list of tracks in the current folder.
- The currently playing track (if any) is not guaranteed to be visible.
- No keyboard shortcut to bring the current track into view is exposed.

[Before screenshot (ASCII approximation)]
Nothingness Browser - Current Folder
| Left margin | Track 1             |
| Track 2             |
| Track 3 (playing)     |
| Track 4             |
| ...                   |
Current track (playing) is off-screen.

After (Ctrl+G is bound to the “bring current track into view” action and is visible to assistive tech)
- The same browser view as before, but with a keyboard action now available.
- Press Ctrl+G to bring the current playing track into view; the page keeps showing the same folder and the target row scrolls into view.

[After screenshot (ASCII approximation)]
Nothingness Browser - Current Folder
| Left margin | Track 1             |
| Track 2             |
| Track 3 (playing)     |  <= current track scrolls into view
| Track 4             |
| ...                   |
Current track is now visible within the current folder.

Notes and caveats
- The change is Linux-focused via keyboard shortcuts, aligning with the “accessible action” requirement without introducing Android/iOS-specific UI changes.
- If you’d like an on-screen affordance as well (a hidden/visible button that triggers the same action for users who can’t use keyboard shortcuts), we can add a small Semantics-enabled button next to the browser header that calls the same VoidBrowserController.scrollToTrack(path) logic.
- The patch avoids exposing the action when there’s no current track path (per your requirement).

If you want, I can provide a concrete patch snippet (with exact edits for lib/widgets/void_screen.dart) or a small on-screen button variant in addition to the keyboard shortcut.
